cands.name: James Linderholm

money.note: Covers January 2023 on, primary and general. Party-committee lines are often in-kind staff and mail.
money.source: Alabama Fair Campaign Practices Act system, downloaded Nov 5, 2026

cands.bio: Founder of Huntsville Gymnastics, which he has run for over three decades with locations in Huntsville, Madison and Hampton Cove. He studied law at Oxford and practiced in London and Birmingham, Alabama. Democratic candidate for Alabama House District 20 in 2026. He has held no elected office.

endorsements.text: Alabama AFL-CIO is listed among his 2026 endorsements.
Persist Alabama is listed among his 2026 endorsements.

cands.gaps: He has no record in public office, so there are no votes or official actions to report. We found no stated position from him on data centers, homestead property taxes, limits on investor or foreign land buyers, slowing growth, immigration or H-1B, police pay, guns, abortion, or school vouchers and charters. His campaign materials say teachers are the most important resource and that education funding should be restored, but we found no specific teacher pay raise or school choice position. His infrastructure page was not opened, only its summary. We found no documented controversies and no foreign ties. We could not confirm his exact birthplace within Illinois, the years he practiced law, his bar admission, or the year he moved to Alabama before Huntsville.

cands.name: James Lomax

money.note: Covers January 2023 on, primary and general. Party-committee lines are often in-kind staff and mail.
money.source: Alabama Fair Campaign Practices Act system, downloaded Nov 5, 2026

cands.bio: Republican state representative for Alabama House District 20 (Huntsville) since November 2022. Worked in commercial real estate, including as vice president of asset management and leasing at Corporate Office Properties Trust. Holds degrees from UAH and Lipscomb University. Lives in Huntsville.
cands.gaps: We found no documented stances from Lomax on data centers, homestead property taxes, foreign or investor land purchases, growth and land protection, H-1B or immigration enforcement, gun policy, abortion, or school choice and teacher pay. We could not confirm his birthplace, where he spent his childhood beyond his Huntsville high school, or when he moved to Alabama. His campaign site mentions an Alabama Farmers Federation endorsement and news stories about a dispute with his primary opponent Mo Brooks, but only as headlines, so we left them out. He did not complete Ballotpedia's candidate survey in 2022 or 2026, and Ballotpedia lists no endorsements for him.
